notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch + HTML parsing) used throughout; site fully reachable, no blocks. robots.txt checked first: only disallows '*/pages/configurator?*=*' (no Claude-specific disallow). Discovery method: full collections sitemap (https://fermliving.com/sitemap_collections_1.xml, ~200 collection URLs enumerated) cross-checked against the live main navigation (Shop/Inspiration/Rooms/Professionals megamenus, extracted from SSR HTML) and an internal-search discrimination check. Live main nav currently has NO holiday-named entry anywhere (Shop, Inspiration, Rooms, Professionals megamenus fully enumerated, zero 'holiday' occurrences) -- the site appears to unlink its Holiday collections outside the winter campaign window (checked 2026-09-04, off-season). However the collections themselves are live, indexed in the sitemap, return 200, use the standard Shopify PLP template (product grid with data-product-id cards, pagination, 'Sort by' control) and carry site-authored holiday-specific titles/meta descriptions, so they are included as genuine seasonal PLPs per the rules (sitemap-based discovery is an explicit, valid discovery path; a page need not be in the currently-active nav to be a real category). Found collections: 'The Holiday Collection' (title 'The Holiday Collection', meta: 'This holiday season, Ferm Living introduces a collection...'), 'Holiday Decorations' (meta: 'Decorate for the holiday with Ferm Living'), 'Holiday Candles and Candleholders' (meta explicitly says 'Count down to Christmas or light up some beautiful candles...' -- this is the clearest evidence the site's 'Holiday' language = the Christmas/winter-holiday season, consistent with rules §3's listing of 'Holiday Decor/Holiday Decorations' under the Christmas vocabulary), and 'Decorate the Holiday Home' (an Earl-of-East collaboration edit, meta: '...embrace the festive season...', also has real 'Sort by' control and a product grid, not a pure editorial page). Verified by product-ID-set comparison that 'Holiday Decorations' (70 items) and 'Holiday Candles and Candleholders' (69 items) are both 100% subsets of 'The Holiday Collection' (145 items via pagination: 48+48+48+1) -- per the shared parent/child rule, 'The Holiday Collection' is recorded as a grouping row rather than double-counted; it has ~9 unique products beyond the two subcategories (not broken into their own subcategory by the site) which are only reflected in the parent's total, not a separate row. 'Decorate the Holiday Home' (33 items, single page, no pagination) overlaps only partially with The Holiday Collection (25 of 33 products shared, 8 unique to the Earl of East edit) so it is NOT a subset and is kept as its own distinct row rather than nested under the parent. Also found 'Back to School' (42 items, single page, no pagination, meta: 'A new school year is the perfect time to refresh children's spaces...') which is explicitly listed in the ruleset's 'other genuine seasonal events' vocabulary; recorded as its own standalone category (unrelated to Christmas/Holiday). Excluded: 'Sale - Holiday' (/collections/sale-holiday) -- a Sale-branded page per the shared marketing exclusion list, also 0 products currently; 'Gift Guide' pages (gift-guide-someone-special, gift-guide-kids, gift-guide-host, gift-guide-wedding) -- explicitly excluded marketing/editorial pages; 'AW25 Collection' / 'SS26 Collection' -- confirmed via title+meta these are fashion-style seasonal PRODUCT-LAUNCH collections (design seasons), not calendar holiday/festival categories; 'Boutique Events' and 'Campaign spots' -- confirmed non-seasonal via title check; '/collections/christmas-decorations' -- returns HTTP 301 to homepage (a retired/deleted collection slug, not a live category). Checked for other holidays: no Halloween, Diwali, Valentine's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, New Year, or Indian-festival collection exists anywhere in the sitemap or nav. Ran a discrimination check on internal search (confirmed search markup and result-count parsing against a known term 'vase' = 114 results) then searched christmas/halloween/diwali/valentine/easter: 'christmas' returns 148 results (consistent with the Holiday collections found), but 'halloween', 'valentine', 'easter' all return 0 results (genuine absence, not a flat-N false-absence pattern), and 'diwali' returns 11 results that on inspection are unrelated fuzzy-search noise (an 'Aquart Shower', 'Innerglow' lamp, and a Seletti gift card -- none Diwali-related), confirming no genuine Diwali category. No local-language (Danish/French/German) seasonal navigation found beyond the collections already captured (locale sitemaps mirror the same collection set). No PDPs were crawled for classification; only collection-level PLP HTML and titles/meta were inspected.
